newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telefonica to sign digital TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica to sign digital TV deal.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica is close to signing an agreement with a number of television channels to provide a platform for digital television in Spain, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
"Negotiations are very advanced and probably Telefonica's board will approve the deal tomorrow," the spokesman said.

Daily El Pais reported on Tuesday that the platform's capital would be 20 billion pesetas ($155.7 million), of which Telefonica would control 36 percent, with Spanish stations TVE and Antena 3 and Mexico's Televisa holding 17 percent each.
The remaining 13 percent will be divided between four regional television stations, including TV3, Canal 9 and the Galician region's TVG.
Digital TV could be transmitted from March 1997, according to a provisional calendar.
Telefonica said at the end of October that it planned to create a new company to launch digital television by satellite, offering more than 150 channels in Spain.
Investment necessary for the TV launch would be around 24 billion pesetas over the next three years, Telefonica said.
The service would cost subscribers 2,500 to 3,000 pesetas per month for the basic service of 15 channels and renting a decoder.
